content.tile_rule: tile in row r and column c is D (diamond) when r + c is even and S (upright square) when r + c is odd

D.shape: square of side 0.62 rotated 45 degrees about the tile centre

S.shape: axis-aligned square of side 0.66 about the tile centre

diagram.manim_description: On a plain white (BG) 16:9 canvas of 16 by 9 units (1920 by 1080 px, 120 px per unit, y up), draw one square panel filled MARK_FILL with no outline, side 8.32 units, centred on the canvas: x from 3.84 to 12.16 and y from 0.34 to 8.66. Inside the panel draw 9 rows by 9 columns of white (BG) tiles on a pitch of 0.88 units. The centre of the tile in column c (1 to 9, left to right) has x = 4.48 + 0.88 (c - 1), that is 4.48, 5.36, 6.24, 7.12, 8.00, 8.88, 9.76, 10.64, 11.52. The centre of the tile in row r (1 to 9, top to bottom) has y = 8.02 - 0.88 (r - 1), that is 8.02, 7.14, 6.26, 5.38, 4.50, 3.62, 2.74, 1.86, 0.98. The tile in row r and column c is a diamond (type D) when r + c is even and an upright square (type S) when r + c is odd, so rows 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 read D S D S D S D S D from left to right and rows 2, 4, 6 and 8 read S D S D S D S D S. Type S is an axis-aligned square of side 0.66 centred on the tile centre. Type D is a square of side 0.62 turned through 45 degrees about the tile centre, a diamond whose four corners lie 0.438 units to the left, right, above and below the centre. Cut every tile, D and S alike, into a lattice of 5 by 5 equal tiny squares by 4 equally spaced lines in each of its two side directions (the lattice of a D tile is turned with the diamond); an S cell has side 0.132 units and a D cell has side 0.124 units. Draw the outline of every tile and all its lattice lines in INK with a 2 px stroke, so every tiny square is a separate white cell and can be counted. Draw no text, no numbers, no brackets, no counts, no totals and no letters anywhere. The picture holds 41 D tiles and 40 S tiles, 81 tiles in all.
must_not_show: any count or total: no 81, no 25, no 2025, no 9 x 9, no 5 x 5, no braces or brackets marking rows or columns
unequal or partial lattices on the upright tiles as printed on the book page: every tile is a full 5 by 5 lattice
accuracy_checks: 9 rows x 9 columns = 81 tiles; D tiles are the cells with row + column even: 5 x 5 (odd rows) + 4 x 4 (even rows) = 25 + 16 = 41 D tiles; 81 - 41 = 40 S tiles
Every tile (D and S) has exactly 25 tiny squares: 4 internal lines per direction, equally spaced, 5 cells per side
Total tiny squares in the picture = 81 x 25 = 2025 = 3^4 x 5^2 = 45^2 (this total is NOT drawn)
No tile overlaps another tile or leaves the panel: D half-diagonal 0.438 < pitch/2 = 0.44; the diamond corners keep 0.2 units from the panel edge
diagram.alt_text: A light green square panel holds nine rows of nine white tiles, diamond-shaped and upright tiles alternating like a chessboard, and each tile is cut into a five by five grid of tiny squares.
diagram.render_note: Printed picture is nearly square (about 597 by 595 px, dark green panel); it is drawn centred in the 16:9 card with the panel in MARK_FILL (the style tokens have no dark green) and INK lattice lines so each of the 25 cells per tile can be counted. The page raster loses most lattice lines inside the upright tiles (they show only 2 x 2, 2 x 3 or 3 x 3 cells with lines at about 20, 40 and 80 percent); the lines that survive sit at the 5 by 5 positions, the diamonds show the full 5 by 5 lattice, and the LP question and solution state 5 by 5 for every tile.
